turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so I just came in today uh a bit concerned. Uh I've been just having this nasty cough for like the last week and then today morning uh, like I thought the cough would just go away, but today morning I also noticed I'm coughing up some blood.

turns.text: So when did you first start coughing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, so let me think uh I just returned from a mission trip uh to the Philippines 2 weeks ago. This cough started uh just last week, so I would say around six to seven days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And that and the blood in your cough, um that was about yesterday, you said? Or?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Today, OK. OK. Um are you bringing up any phlegm at all, besides the blood?

turns.text: Uh no it's just uh like I saw it on my hand, like there wasn't anything, like my cough is like pretty dry.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, are you short of breath at all?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: 15 pounds OK. Wow, that's a lot, yeah. Um any night sweats?

turns.text: Um no, I don't think so, no.

turns.text: OK, we'll take your temperature today just to make sure. Um any rashes?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, changes in your bowel movements?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, are you otherwise healthy? Do you have any longstanding medical conditions?

turns.text: Um not uh, I don't think so like we um, maybe in the Philippines, we do provide a, so I go on like these mission trips with the Church and um we do sometimes go to the hospital as well.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: But other than that, not since I've been here, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, um those were all the questions that I had for you. Do you have any questions for me?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I I was very worried um uh about the blood. I was just reading some things up and uh, about tuberculosis, so I was really stressed out today.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah so um, that's definitely high on our differential. So, we'll do a couple of things. While you're here in the hospital, we're also going to do a chest X-Ray and or like an AFB smear to see if you have active TB or latent TB. If those come back positive um we will require you to isolate because this uh, because TB is highly infectious and it's airborne. Um so we have a couple of uh, we have like a regimen that we'd put you on. It's called the RIPE medications that we keep you on for two months and then we continue a couple of those for another four months. Um but we will uh keep you here until we have more answers on um like from this TB standpoint. How does that sound?
